name: Ata ẹ̀wà
definition: A Yorùbá medicinal and culinary stew formulated specifically for eating beans, prepared with palm oil, peppers, and digestive aromatics.
exampleYoruba: Mo fẹ́ran ata ẹ̀wà
exampleEnglish: I love beans stew

name: Ayamaṣe
definition: A traditional Yorùbá designer stew infused with fermented locust beans (irú) which possesses antimicrobial and therapeutic cardiovascular properties.
exampleYoruba: Mi ò fẹ́ran Ayamaṣe
exampleEnglish: I don't like ofada stew

name: Àádùn
definition: A roasted cornmeal delicacy prepared with pure red palm oil. Traditionally valued for quick energy restoration and ceremonial rites.
exampleYoruba: Mo ra àádùn ní ojà
exampleEnglish: I bought sweets from the market

name: Àbàrí
definition: Steamed whole-grain maize pudding rich in dietary fibre, formulated to soothe gastric inflammation and digestive discomfort.
exampleYoruba: Mo ra Àbàrí jẹ
exampleEnglish: I bought Àbàrí to eat

name: Àbùlà
definition: Synergistic botanical fusion of gbẹ̀gìrì (cowpea soup) and ewédú (jute mallow), delivering high concentrations of antioxidants, iron, and gut-lubricating mucilage.
exampleYoruba: Wọ́n ń ra àbùlà ní ibí
exampleEnglish: They sell àbùlà here.

name: Àdàlú
definition: A balanced composite porridge of maize and legumes providing complete plant-based proteins, iron, and sustained glycemic stabilization.
exampleYoruba: Àdàlú wàn mi jẹ
exampleEnglish: I love àdàlú

name: Àmàlà dúdú
definition: Dark swallow meal crafted from sun-dried, fermented Dioscorea yam peels. Highly regarded in indigenous healing for diabetic management and low glycemic response.
exampleYoruba: Mo jẹ àmàlà dúdú ní àná
exampleEnglish: I ate black àmàlà yesterday

name: Àpọ̀n
definition: Viscous draw soup derived from wild African bush mango seeds (Irvingia gabonensis), documented for blood glucose management, weight regulation, and pain mitigation.
exampleYoruba: Mi ò fẹ́ran obẹ̀ Àpọ̀n gan-an.
exampleEnglish: I don't really like ogbono soup.

name: Àsáró
definition: Coarsely mashed yam porridge stewed in unrefined palm oil, dried fish, and anti-inflammatory peppers. Prescribed for recuperation and postpartum nourishment.
exampleYoruba: Àsáró jẹ́ óúnjẹ àráàlú pàtàkì lójúmọ́ ní ilé wa
exampleEnglish: Àsáró is a Wednesday morning special in my home

name: Bọ̀lì
definition: Charcoal-roasted unripe or semi-ripe plantain, rich in potassium, complex carbohydrates, and resistant starches supportive of renal health.
exampleYoruba: Bọ̀lì ti wón ń ta lọ́nà dùn gan-an
exampleEnglish: The roasted plantain sold on the street is really delicious

name: Dòdò
definition: Golden pan-fried ripe plantain slices, rich in Vitamin A, Vitamin C, and natural carbohydrates.
exampleYoruba: Mo fẹ́ dòdò pẹ̀lú ẹ̀wà
exampleEnglish: I want fried plantain with beans

name: Dùndún
definition: Crisp-fried tuber slices seasoned with salt, eaten as an energizing staple alongside herbal pepper dips.
exampleYoruba: Dùndún àti ẹyin dín-dín ni mo jẹ lárọ̀ yìí
exampleEnglish: I had fried yam and egg this morning

name: Èbà
definition: Fermented cassava meal (garri) reconstituted with boiling water. Contains probiotic fermentation acids that support gut microbiota.
exampleYoruba: Èbà àti obẹ̀ ẹ̀gúsí ni mo fẹ́
exampleEnglish: I want eba and egusi soup

name: Ẹ̀gúsí
definition: Melon seed preparation (Citrullus lanatus) packed with essential fatty acids, tocopherols (Vitamin E), and zinc, celebrated for skin vitality and tissue repair.
exampleYoruba: Obẹ̀ ẹ̀gúsí ni mo fẹ́ran jù lọ
exampleEnglish: Egusi soup is my favourite

name: Ẹ̀fọ́ rírò
definition: Therapeutic vegetable soup simmered with soko (Celosia argentea) or tete (Amaranthus), providing abundant bioavailable iron, folate, and calcium.
exampleYoruba: Ẹ̀fọ́ rírò ìyá mi dùn gan-an
exampleEnglish: My mother's vegetable soup is really delicious

name: Ewédú
definition: Jute leaf mucilage (Corchorus olitorius) boiled and whisked into a draw soup. Highly revered for postpartum recovery, anti-aging, and gentle gastrointestinal easing.
exampleYoruba: Ewédú àti gbẹ̀gìrì l'a ó jẹ
exampleEnglish: We will eat ewedu and gbegiri

name: Fúfú
definition: Fermented wet cassava dough kneaded into an elastic swallow, easily digested following extensive microbial fermentation.
exampleYoruba: Fúfú àti obẹ̀ ọ̀gbọ́nọ̀ ni mo jẹ
exampleEnglish: I ate fufu and ogbono soup

name: Gbẹ̀gìrì
definition: Dehulled brown cowpea broth whipped into a velvety soup, containing concentrated vegetable protein, dietary potassium, and natural folate.
exampleYoruba: Gbẹ̀gìrì ìyá mi lẹwà gan-an
exampleEnglish: My mother's gbegiri is very smooth

name: Iyán
definition: Mortar-pounded white yam, celebrated as the ceremonial apex of Yorùbá gastronomy and convalescent rehabilitation.
exampleYoruba: Iyán ni oúnjẹ ọba
exampleEnglish: Pounded yam is the food of kings

name: Kòkòrò
definition: Crunchy baked or fried maize snack flavored with ginger and spices, promoting digestive saliva production.
exampleYoruba: Kòkòrò dùn gan-an
exampleEnglish: Kokoro is very tasty

name: Làfún
definition: Fine sun-dried cassava flour swallow with light consistency, naturally gluten-free and gentle on the intestinal tract.
exampleYoruba: Làfún àti obẹ̀ ewédú ni mo fẹ́
exampleEnglish: I want lafun and ewedu soup

name: Mọ́ìn-mọ́ìn
definition: Steamed savory bean pudding blended with peppers and onions, wrapped in miracle leaves (Thaumatococcus daniellii) which infuse polyphenol antioxidants.
exampleYoruba: Mọ́ìn-mọ́ìn àti ẹ̀kọ ni mo fẹ́
exampleEnglish: I want moin-moin and eko

name: Ògì
definition: Fermented cereal pudding (maize, sorghum, or millet) loaded with lactic acid bacteria, prized across Yorùbá medicine for infant weaning, fever recovery, and hydration.
exampleYoruba: Ògì àti àkàrà ni oúnjẹ àárọ̀ mi
exampleEnglish: Pap and akara is my breakfast

name: Ọ̀fàdà
definition: Unpolished, unbleached local indigenous rice retaining its nutrient-dense bran layer and germ, rich in thiamine, magnesium, and resistant fiber.
exampleYoruba: Ọ̀fàdà àti ayamaṣe ni mo fẹ́
exampleEnglish: I want ofada rice and designer stew

name: Pẹlẹbẹ
definition: Sun-crisped thin yam slivers lightly salted, used traditionally as an appetite stimulant and convenient travel ration.
exampleYoruba: Mo fẹ́ pẹlẹbẹ yán
exampleEnglish: I want crispy yam chips

name: Sùyà
definition: Skewered lean meat seasoned with yaji—a therapeutic blend of ginger, alligator pepper, cloves, and groundnut cake that promotes metabolic warmth.
exampleYoruba: Sùyà àlẹ́ ana dùn gan-an
exampleEnglish: Last night's suya was really delicious

name: Àkàrà
definition: Golden bean fritters whipped with air and fried in fresh oil, serving as an easily assimilated high-protein breakfast and celebratory food.
exampleYoruba: Àkàrà gbígbóná dùn jù lọ
exampleEnglish: Hot akara is the tastiest
